overview.title: Where the work still happens
overview.p1: Tetouan has long been known for craft skill. In the artisan quarter and workshop streets you see leather, textiles and other trades practised at a human scale — not only sold as finished souvenirs.
overview.p2: The best visits are unhurried: watch, ask permission before photos, and buy when something is genuinely well made. Guides who know open workshops save time.
overview.p3: Morning is practical; many workshops wind down later. Combine with the main medina souks the same day.

q1.question: Can I photograph workshops?
q1.answer: Ask first. Some artisans welcome it; others prefer privacy.

q2.question: Do I have to buy?
q2.answer: No. Looking with respect is fine. Buy only what you want.

q3.question: Guide useful?
q3.answer: Yes for finding active workshops and fair introductions.

q4.question: Best time?
q4.answer: Morning when workshops are fully open.

q5.question: Shipping?
q5.answer: Discuss with the seller; not all stalls arrange international post.

food.title: Eat around the workshops
food.p1: Snack in the medina; save a sit-down meal for after you finish shopping.
food.p2: Keep hands free while moving between workshops.
